display.purpose: Section heads and the cover headline. Expanded (wdth 118) black caps, negatively tracked. The masthead voice.

headline.purpose: One step below display, used for the award section.

pull.purpose: The single sentence opening the stylist feature. Sentence case at wdth 108, which is what separates it from a heading.

title.purpose: Service entry names, margin notes, boxed sub-heads, drawer links.

base.purpose: Page default. Captions and small copy step down from here.

label.purpose: The magazine's caption voice: tracked small caps for cover lines, fact keys, nav and footer links.

action.purpose: Buttons and call targets. Wide-tracked caps in a hard rectangle.

navLabel.purpose: Nav and footer links, review citations, compact call button.

micro.purpose: Footer fine print and the colophon box note.

caption.purpose: Plate captions in the feature well.

smallBody.purpose: Service entry copy, fact values, tightened prose.

coverHeadline.purpose: The masthead line on the cover.

marginNote.purpose: The heading beside the offset plate.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: The only expressive curve in the build. Used for the page turn, the drawer, the bar and button state.

motion.name: page-turn
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: the opener plate wipes open from the gutter. Scoped to .plate.opener alone.

motion.name: beat
motion.purpose: Caption tier. A 12px rise and fade set one beat after the plate so the wipe still reads as the event.

motion.name: thumb-zoom
motion.purpose: Contents entry thumbnail scales to 1.06 on hover. Nothing else in the row moves.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button, link and bar state changes. Deliberately unremarkable so the page turn stays the only motion event.

components.name: Primary Action
components.description: The call action. Chalk fill on ink; hover removes the fill rather than tinting it.

components.name: Line Action
components.description: Secondary action. Hairline outline on ink; hover fills chalk.

components.name: Nav Call Button
components.description: Always-visible call target in the fixed bar. Collapses to a 46px icon square below 700px.

components.name: Nav Link
components.description: Section link in the fixed bar. A transparent bottom border becomes gold on hover.

components.name: Plate and Caption
components.description: The signature unit of the feature well: an aspect-ratio image frame with a gold category word and a caption sentence beneath it.

components.name: Contents Entry
components.description: The services row on the paper section. A magazine contents line, not a service card: thumbnail, title, description, hairline rules, no fill and no border.

narrative.overview:
The site is a printed fashion issue, not a salon website. Her finished hair is the entire argument, so every structural decision hands the page back to the photographs: a full-bleed cover plate with the logo lockup as masthead, a feature well of plates with numbered captions, a contents page for services, a colophon for booking. There is no salon-template hero, no icon-card service grid, and none of the cream/serif/terracotta vocabulary of the site it replaced.

The ground is near-black ink with chalk text, broken exactly once by a paper-white reading section. Colour arrives from the photography and nowhere else; the only manufactured warm value is the gold lifted out of the client's existing logo, spent on caption numbers, fact keys, focus rings and link hovers. Structure is carried by hairline rules and grid alignment, never by cards, panels, radii or shadows. One typeface does all of it: Archivo variable, worked through width, weight, case, tracking and scale.

The build is phone-first by construction. It is read at night on a small screen, so the display sizes are clamped against viewport width, the cover headline narrows its width axis rather than shrinking, and every text pair clears WCAG AA (measured floor 5.27:1, dimmed ink on paper).
keyCharacteristics: One grotesque, five widths, no second family
Ink ground, chalk text, one paper section, one gold chrome
Square corners everywhere; there is no radius token in the file
Hairline rules and grid alignment instead of cards
Photography supplies all colour; type never competes with it
One authored motion moment, gated so content is visible by default

rules.name: The Photograph Supplies the Colour Rule
rules.body: No hue enters the palette that is not already in a plate. If a surface needs warmth, crop a photograph into it rather than tinting it.

rules.name: The Gold Is Ink, Not Paint Rule
rules.body: Gold is used as a foreground mark at small sizes only: caption numbers, fact keys, hover underlines, focus rings. It never fills a shape, never becomes a button, and never appears at display scale.

rules.name: The One Paper Section Rule
rules.body: Light ground is a deliberate interruption in the sequence, used for the reading sections (contents, letters). A third and fourth paper section would turn the interruption into a stripe pattern and destroy it.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo does every job. Any new hierarchy tier is produced by moving wdth, wght, case, tracking or scale. Adding a second family is the one change that breaks this system outright.

rules.name: The Width Axis Yields First Rule
rules.body: When display type will not hold its line count on a small screen, narrow the width axis before you cut the size. The cover headline drops from wdth 116 to wdth 100 below 560px and keeps its scale.

rules.name: The Caps Are For Structure Rule
rules.body: Uppercase marks the frame, headings, labels, buttons, navigation. Anything that is actually read as a sentence, including the pull quote, stays in sentence case.

rules.name: The Caption Returns to the Column Rule
rules.body: An image may break the column; its caption may not. Full-bleed plates always re-enter min(1240px, 100% - 2 x gut) so the caption line hangs on the same left edge as the body text.

rules.name: The Gutter Is the Only Margin Rule
rules.body: Page margin, bar padding and cover inset all read --gut. Never hard-code an edge inset.

rules.name: The One-Border Rule
rules.body: Elevation is declared once. A surface gets a 1px border or a ground change, never a border plus a shadow.

rules.name: The Local Scrim Rule
rules.body: When type on a photograph is not legible, give that block its own radial ground. Do not darken the global gradient; the plate is the argument and dimming it costs more than it buys.

rules.name: The Square Corner Rule
rules.body: Radius is zero throughout. A rounded corner in this world reads immediately as an import from a different site.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separation is a 1px rule or nothing. No dividers thicker than 1px, no filled separator bars, no card outlines pretending to be containers.

dos: Do produce new hierarchy by moving Archivo's wdth and wght axes. The named widths in use are 100 (body, labels, actions), 108 (pull), 112 (titles), 116 and 118 (display).
Do narrow the width axis before reducing display size on small screens.
Do keep every corner square and every separation a 1px hairline.
Do give a text block over a photograph its own local radial ground rather than darkening the global scrim.
Do let a plate break the column and bring its caption back into min(1240px, 100% - 2 x gut).
Do spend gold only as a small foreground mark: caption categories, fact keys, hover underlines, focus rings.
Do gate any new motion behind the motion root class so content is visible when JS or IntersectionObserver is absent.
Do assemble contact addresses at runtime; keep them out of the markup.
Do hold every text pair above 4.5:1. The current floor is 5.27:1 (dimmed ink on paper); do not add a dimmer tier under it.
donts: Don't introduce a second typeface, a serif, or a script face for accents.
Don't add border-radius, box-shadow, or a card surface. A surface gets one border or one ground change, never both.
Don't invent a colour. New hue enters through photography, or not at all.
Don't use gold as a fill, a button, a rule, or at display scale.
Don't add a third or fourth paper section; the light ground works because it interrupts.
Don't turn services into an icon grid or a card deck. They are contents lines on rules.
Don't extend the clip-path wipe to other plates. One authored moment; everything else arrives quietly.
Don't centre body composition. The cover masthead is the only centred element in the build.
